lesson_title: Ceilings Make Queues, Floors Make Piles
hook_text: Pin a price down and a queue appears. Pin it up and a pile appears. Every time.
clip_script: Markets are games, and games need referees. Watch what happens when the referee blows the whistle. Move one: the state pins a price DOWN so essentials stay affordable — and sellers offer less while buyers want more. The gap becomes a queue: rationing, first-come-first-served, and a back door where the desperate pay extra anyway. Ceilings make queues. Move two: the state pins a price UP so producers survive — and now sellers offer more than buyers take. Floors make piles: surpluses somebody must buy, store or ship out. And the minimum wage? A floor under people instead of produce — real protection for the worker who keeps the job, and the honest sentence adds: at a higher price for labour, some employers hire fewer hands. Both halves, always. That is the whole trick of this topic: every intervention helps somebody on purpose and costs somebody by consequence — and the marks go to the learner who can see the consequence coming before the examiner asks.
visual_style: A referee's whistle over a stylised market; a price bar pressed down as a queue of figures stretches off-screen; the bar pushed up as crates stack into a tower; a scale balancing a raised wage against empty chairs.
mood: Crisp, fair-minded, eye-opening — rules and consequences in plain sight.
pacing: Two symmetrical beats for ceiling and floor, a thoughtful slowdown on the minimum wage, firm landing on the both-halves rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision sweep: the referee's four moves, the road from barter to industry, and the queue at the gate.
